rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promised guidance to Adam and his descendants and made the same promise to Iblis and his descendants.
rows.anchor: that He will send guidance to them, He has also made this very promise with Iblīs and His progeny.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an states that messengers were sent to the jinn as well as to humankind.
rows.anchor: messengers were also sent to the jinn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah opens by presenting the Qur’an as divine mercy and teaching; human creation and speech make people fit to learn through revelation rather than punishment.
rows.anchor: The sūrah begins with the declaration that the Qur’ ān is a manifestation of the graciousness of the Almighty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse points to signs within and around people, repeatedly warning humans and jinn to reflect and asking how many signs they will deny.
rows.anchor: the various signs in the world around man and those within him are pointed to and two of the Almighty’s creations – men and jinn– are repeatedly warned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first signs emphasized show that God cherishes justice and rejects whatever violates justice and equity.
rows.anchor: First and foremost are mentioned those signs and manifestations which point to the fact that the Almighty greatly cherishes justice and does not approve anything contrary to justice and equity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vast system of earthly sustenance entails that people will answer for its blessings: the deserving will be rewarded and the deserving of punishment punished.
rows.anchor: the tremendous and extremely vast system of sustenance which the Almighty has established on the earth entails that man shall one day be held accountable

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity and jinn were created from clay and fire, and God can readily create them again.
rows.anchor: it is the Almighty who has created men and jinn from fire and clay and He can easily create them a second time

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God controls the whole universe as Lord of East and West; every rising and setting occurs by His permission.
rows.anchor: This whole Universe is under His control; He is the Lord of the East and the West. Whatever rises, rises with His permission and whatever sets, sets with His permission.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe’s conflicting elements work harmoniously toward a higher collective purpose, showing that one sovereign will governs them.
rows.anchor: the conflicting elements in the universe are in harmony with one another to fulfil a greater purpose which is over and above their creation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered survival of opposing elements shows that one supreme, omnipotent power controls and harmonizes them for the universe’s welfare.
rows.anchor: the universe would have been destroyed by a clash between its conflicting elements. That it is surviving is ample testimony to the fact that a single supreme and omnipotent power controls it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God is immortal; all other beings perish.
rows.anchor: God alone is immortal and all the rest are mortal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything besides God depends on Him, the sole provider of needs.
rows.anchor: all except the Almighty are needy and He is the only one who fulfils their needs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the certain Day of Judgment people cannot flee; foreheads expose sinners, who are seized and thrown into Hell.
rows.anchor: no evidence will be needed to convict a criminal as his forehead will bear witness to his sins. He will then be grabbed by his forehead and feet and flung into Hell.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah distinguishes the characteristics of Paradise for the muqarrabīn from those for the asḥāb al-yamīn.
rows.anchor: the muqarrabīn shall receive are delineated, followed by the features and characteristics of the Paradise which the asḥāb al-yamīn will be blessed with

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revealing the Qur’an for instruction is a special mercy: it reforms mistaken beliefs and deeds so people can succeed in this life and the next, whereas they demand punishment.
rows.anchor: He could have sent punishment as per their demand; however, out of His great mercy He blessed them with a benevolent scripture

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation and speech imply that God intends to teach people through a guidance-giving scripture rather than torment.
rows.anchor: the creation of man and his abilities also require that instead of torment, a scripture of guidance be sent down.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech entails intellect: people can move between particulars and principles, reason, infer, and form opinions.
rows.anchor: man has intellect, he can derive principles from parts and vice versa and simulate parts from principles.

rows.speaker: Aristotle
rows.claim: Aristotle regards this intellectual ability as what distinguishes humans from animals; without it a person is merely a two-legged animal.
rows.anchor: Aristotle regards this ability of man as one which distinguishes him from animals.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who insist on seeing a reality before believing, despite being able to reason, are no better than animals.
rows.anchor: those who, instead of understanding a reality on the basis of reasoning, insist that they will only believe in it after seeing it are no less than animals

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regular, punctual paths of the sun and moon are signs that teach people to obey their Creator’s laws.
rows.anchor: the sun and the moon adhere to their paths with such punctuality and discipline. There is never a discrepancy even of a second.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon remain within their distinct ordained paths and never intrude on one another’s course.
rows.anchor: Never does the sun exceed its ordained path to intrude into the path ordained for the moon nor does the moon intrude into the path ordained for the sun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon’s obedience to limits is called taqwā in religious terminology and teaches humans to abide by God’s laws.
rows.anchor: After mentioning how the sun and the moon abide by the limits ordained for them and which in religious parlance is called taqwā

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people break the laws God has established throughout the universe and spread anarchy, they will be punished.
rows.anchor: If man breaks these laws and dares spread anarchy in this world, why would He not punish him?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stars and trees prostrate before their Creator, calling people to submit and worship in obedience.
rows.anchor: the stars of the heavens and trees of the earth: they bow down before their Creator and through this practice of theirs call upon man

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some interpreters take najm to mean small plants, thorny trees, or creepers; Islahi regards this as far-fetched.
rows.anchor: Probably, they were not able to understand the purpose of mentioning trees with stars and for this reason they had to make this far-fetched interpretation.

rows.speaker: Mujāhid, Qatādah and Ḥasan
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Qatādah, and Ḥasan take najm in its conventional sense of stars; Ibn Kathīr supports this interpretation.
rows.anchor: Mujāhid, Qatādah and Ḥasan interpret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stars and trees share attributes and are rightly mentioned together, showing harmony between heaven and earth under one Creator; both prostrate to Him.
rows.anchor: there exists great commonality in the attributes of the two.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the immense sky like a roof without columns and made it so balanced that it has no visible fault, as other passages also affirm.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has raised this unfathomable roof without any columns. No one can have an idea of its vastness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s balance is maintained by invisible gravitational columns.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has used gravitational columns which cannot be observed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmic balance reveals God’s character and demands that people uphold justice and equity; transgression brings disorder and punishment in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: it is to this system of justice and fairness the Qur’ ān is calling man

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honest weighing and measuring apply the cosmic principle in daily life; cheating is social disorder and attacks the foundation of the world God built.
rows.anchor: they should weigh and measure with full honesty and not weigh less. While commenting on the anecdote of the Prophet Shu‘ayb’s people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an uses positive and negative formulations when disobedience has dangerous consequences, underscoring the great significance of just weighing and measuring.
rows.anchor: this style is adopted at instances when not obeying the real directive can lead to very dangerous consequences.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A society or nation that disrupts the command to weigh justly creates disorder throughout society.
rows.anchor: a nation which disrupts and disobeys this directive creates disorder in the whole society.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired terms present heaven as a raised roof and earth as a laid floor, making a comfortable abode equipped with light, heat, food, fragrance, and beauty.
rows.anchor: the heavens were raised high like a roof and the earth was spread out like a floor so that this arrangement could become a comfortable abode for His creatures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning grain, flowers, and fruit shows that God provides for aesthetic taste, delicacies, and adornment as well as basic nourishment.
rows.anchor: specially mentioned to point to the fact that the Almighty has not merely provided man fodder to fill his belly

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The described coverings around grain and dates display elaborate providence, obliging people to gratitude and reminding them of accountability.
rows.anchor: He has not just tossed grain and fruit towards man; He has elaborately packed each and every grain and fruit in an amazing manner.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some interpreters explain rīḥān as leaves; Islahi rejects this because the word is not used that way in Arabic and the context does not require it.
rows.anchor: this word has not been used in this meaning in Arabic nor is there any occasion for it to be used here in this meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation of rīḥān as leaves is unattested in Arabic and unnecessary in context; flowers have a specific role alongside food.
rows.anchor: this word has not been used in this meaning in Arabic nor is there any occasion for it to be used here in this meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Flowers are mentioned for a particular reason explained in the account of God’s provision of taste, beauty, and fragrance.
rows.anchor: there is a particular reason for this mention, as I have explained above.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question is the sūrah’s most important verse; it directly rebukes Quraysh and jinn rejecters allied against the call of truth and challenges them that it will prevail.
rows.anchor: this campaign of rejection had gained great impetus and the devils among men and jinn had joined hands and were trying their best to defeat the call of the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah was revealed when Quraysh hostility peaked, and the situation called for addressing them together with the jinn, whose devils specially supported them.
rows.anchor: it was revealed in that phase of the Makkan period in which the Quraysh were at the peak of their obduracy and hostility.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude for divine favors and accountability to their provider are natural duties; denying either obligation amounts to denying those favors.
rows.anchor: Expressing gratitude on favours to someone who has granted these favours and having a sense of accountability to the providence of God are natural requirements of human nature.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh and jinn are rebuked for denying blessings that remind them of accountability, despite the signs visible in earlier peoples and their own lives.
rows.anchor: on every people before them they can witness the favours of their Lord which remind them (ie. the Quraysh and the jinn) of a day of accountability

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminders of human and jinn creation point to resurrection: the original material and God’s creative power remain available, so denying re-creation is inconsistent.
rows.anchor: they should not remain under the misconception that their Lord is unable to recreate them after creating them once

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalṣāl means pure mud.
rows.anchor: refers to pure mud and

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fakhkhār refers to mud which becomes dry.
rows.anchor: which becomes dry like a

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an describes human origins through fluid, mud, smelly kneaded clay, and dry mud, followed by offspring beginning from sperm; these stages show divine power and purposeful creation.
rows.anchor: The final phase mentioned is that from a drop of sperm man’s offspring is initiated.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gradual formation and nurturing of human beings demonstrates wisdom, purpose, and the ability to do anything.
rows.anchor: the all-knowing and all-wise God Who can create man from a cell formed from mire can do everything; nothing is beyond Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marij means the flame or essence of fire, just as humanity is made from the essence of mud; the jinn’s stages are omitted because they are alien to human comprehension.
rows.anchor: The reason for this is that these phases are of an entirely different nature comprehending which would have been difficult for man.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After people see signs of power in their own creation, the repeated question challenges them to explain why re-creation for judgment seems impossible.
rows.anchor: when they observe these majesties and manifestations of power and wisdom in their own existence, why then do they regard it to be far-fetched that God will create them again

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone owns and rules the East and West; no one lies beyond His dominion or shares it.
rows.anchor: Neither is there anyone outside His dominion nor does anyone have a share in it. He alone is the owner of all the East and the West.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sovereignty over all the East and West demonstrates His power to recreate people, as 70:40–41 says.
rows.anchor: Nay! I swear by the Lord who is the Master of all the vastness of the East and the West that We can create them in a better form

rows.speaker: our exegetes
rows.claim: Many exegetes take the dual Easts and Wests to mean the sunrise and sunset points of winter and summer; Islahi calls this unnatural.
rows.anchor: east and west of the winters and the summer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seasonal interpretation of the duals is unnatural; singular, dual, and plural forms differ little in meaning, with dual marking the two edges and plural their immense extent.
rows.anchor: this however is quite unnatural.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question emphasizes that the East and West are subject to God’s power and majesty.
rows.anchor: such is the power and majesty of God that both East and West are subservient to Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent conflict between nature’s opposites conceals a deep harmony serving a greater end, proving one intention and will governs the universe.
rows.anchor: in every discord exists a deep concord and harmony. Every object together with its opposite comes together to serve a greater cause.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bitter and sweet seas meet but remain separated by an invisible barrier, preserving their distinct natures as evidence of divine unity.
rows.anchor: He puts an invisible curtain between them so that they do meet one another and also remain separate in their own nature.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who infer multiple divine wills from natural conflicts ignore the harmony within discord; the refrain challenges their trust in other deities to save them.
rows.anchor: people who were misled by the apparent conflict between elements and regarded this universe to be a place of different wills and intentions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opposed waters produce a shared benefit in pearls and corals.
rows.anchor: both produce pearls and corals.

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Some exegetes claim pearls and corals come only from bitter water, contrary to the verse’s statement that both produce them.
rows.anchor: have raised the question that pearls and corals only come out of bitter water

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that pearls and corals come only from bitter water is baseless; freshwater pearls from rivers and streams are documented.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, our exegetes have made a baseless claim.

rows.speaker: Encyclopaedia Britannica
rows.claim: The cited reference reports valuable freshwater pearls from North American rivers, British and Bavarian waters, and Chinese freshwater pearling.
rows.anchor: Freshwater mussels in the temperate zone of the Northern Hemisphere have produced pearls of great value.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if pearls are nourished only in bitter water, they can still result from interaction between both waters, as children come from both parents though nourished in the womb.
rows.anchor: things are created from the collaboration of opposites. A child is born from a mother and a father.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The placement and context of the repeated question make its implication clear.
rows.anchor: After this, occurs the repetitive verse. Its context and placement is evident.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Massive ships laden with cargo float while lighter objects sink, displaying divine power and harmony between opposing elements.
rows.anchor: an object as heavy as a ship loaded with thousands of tons of cargo sails on water and does not drown.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about ships in God’s control means that only God has authority to create harmony between discordant elements.
rows.anchor: here means that creating such harmony between discordant elements is only in the authority of God the one and only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāṭir 35:12 likewise contrasts sweet fresh water and bitter salt water, notes that both yield food and ornaments, and links ships to grateful travel.
rows.anchor: from both you eat fresh meat, and from both you bring out ornaments to wear. And see how the ships plough their course through them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same subject is also treated in Sūrah Shūrā for further detail.
rows.anchor: this subject has been brought up. For more details, it can be consulted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘upon it’ refers back to the earth discussed since verse 10.
rows.anchor: The antecedent of the genitive pronoun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created order, provision, divine wisdom, sovereignty, and harmony entail that all creation will end and only God remain; all will be judged without being able to challenge His decisions or intercede without permission.
rows.anchor: Only the exalted and revered person of God will remain. Everyone will be gathered before Him one day and He will deal with everyone in the manner that person is worthy of.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated phrase ‘Lord of majesty and bounty’ at the end of the sūrah indicates that only God is exalted, revered, and without a partner in these attributes.
rows.anchor: The purpose of mentioning both these words is that only He is exalted in His being and thus only He is worthy of being respected and revered by all.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajh (‘face’) means God’s person because the face, as the highest part, can stand for the whole person.
rows.anchor: face) here signifies the person of God. Face is the most lofty portion of a being; for this reason, at times, it signifies the whole person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refrain recalls that all creatures will perish whether or not they heed the Prophet’s warning, leaving only God.
rows.anchor: whether they hear the warnings of the Prophet or not, one day everyone will be destroyed and only the person of God the Almighty will remain

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true one to whom all beings turn and from whom they ask.
rows.anchor: The implication of this verse is that God is the rea l person to whom everyone turns.
